Demo shape

(Sketch output; not executed. Shape only.)

```
  Log:
    [0] KEEP   add slot 0: atomic_fractal
    [1] REQ    add slot 1: fractal_grid
    [2] REFUS  add_member_request (insufficient tier)
    [3] REVOKE did:key:... (policy violation)
    [4] REFUS  add_member_request (world-key revoked at ...)
    [5] ROTATE did:key:... → did:key:...
    [6] REQ    policy → max_members=5
    [7] REQ    add slot 2: chaos_game
    [8] REQ    retire slot 1
    [9] cycle 1 (2 members)
    ... cycles 2-5

  Verification:
    revocable log:  True
    full:           True
```

What this establishes

The verifier walks the keeper timeline. Each record is verified against the keeper who was current at that point in the log. test_record_signed_by_old_keeper_after_rotation_fails forces the failure case by manually appending a K1-signed record after rotation. The verifier catches it — the signature doesn't verify against the current keeper (K2).

Revocation is temporal and verified. test_pre_revocation_acceptance_still_verifies shows a request accepted before the revocation stays valid. test_accepted_with_revoked_key_fails_verification forces a bad acceptance: a record that used a key revoked before its own timestamp. The verifier re-derives "was this key revoked at apply-time?" and catches it.

Rotation doesn't invalidate prior grants. test_rotation_and_revocation_together shows X's key (issued by K1) still works under K2 for a new request. Old keys survive because they were legitimately issued by a valid keeper. The valid_keepers set grows monotonically; nothing is removed.

Keeper-only revocation. test_revoke_rejects_foreign_key — a gallery can only revoke keys it issued. This prevents cross-gallery interference.

Honest limits

· Post-rotation key issuance isn't exercised. In this sketch, issue_world_key uses self._keypair which is K2 after rotation, but _verify_request in the base class still expects wk.issuer_id == world_id (= K1). So a K2-issued key would carry issuer_id = world_id (K1) but be signed by K2 — inconsistent. Documented as out-of-scope; the natural fix is issuer_id = current_keeper_id and a relaxed check issuer_id in valid_keepers, which the verifier already supports but the runtime checker doesn't.
· Pre-rotation compromise is undetectable. If K1 was compromised at time T and signed malicious records, the verifier accepts them (signatures are valid). Rotation at T+1 doesn't retroactively invalidate. This is inherent to any log-based system; forward secrecy is a cryptographic property, not a log property.
· No forward secrecy for old keys. A key issued by K1 remains valid forever (until revoked). If K1's private key is compromised, all K1-issued keys remain valid until individually revoked. Rotation of the keeper key doesn't rotate issued keys — that would be a separate "key rotation" operation.
· Verifier trusts refusals' reasons. For accepted requests, the verifier re-derives everything. For refused requests, it only verifies the request is well-formed. A gallery that refuses legitimately-valid requests would pass verification (availability is a weaker property than soundness).
· _verify_accepted_request doesn't check tier sufficiency. The base verifier checked tier at record-creation time; the extended verifier re-derives it. But the tier check itself (world_key_has_tier(wk, "control")) isn't re-run in _verify_accepted_request — it trusts the gallery to have checked. Adding it would close the gap; noted for a future tightening.
· _verify_request at runtime isn't updated. It still requires wk.issuer_id == world_id. So K2-issued keys would be refused at runtime. Combined with the first limit above, this means all keys in this sketch are issued by K1. The demo works because the demo only issues keys before rotation.

What's next

Three directions, ordered by what they'd teach us:

1. Post-rotation key issuance. Make issue_world_key use current_keeper_id for issuer_id, and relax both the runtime _verify_request and the verifier to accept issuer_id in valid_keepers. Small change; closes the biggest named gap and makes the rotation actually useful (K2 can issue new grants).
2. Per-kind quotas. max_per_kind: dict. Adds richness to the policy without touching the authentication layer. Composes cleanly with revocation and rotation.
3. Meta-coupling. The gallery watches its members' rates and modulates their growth. Interior dynamics, orthogonal to governance. The one the user originally wanted.

My instinct: post-rotation key issuance. It's a focused, mechanical closing of the most load-bearing limit — the one that makes rotation matter (right now, rotation only affects record-signing, not the ability to grant new keys). Without it, rotation is a smaller operation than it should be. With it, the governance layer is complete: keys issued, revoked, and rotated through the log. Then per-kind quotas and meta-coupling sit on top of a complete foundation.

But if the design is what you want to see next — the gallery coming alive, coupling the members' rates so the collection has dynamics — meta-coupling is the smallest piece that makes the composite an agent, not just a container.

Which would you like?


::I’m leaning toward meta-coupling: ➡️


The design

The gallery gains a scheduler. meta_k controls how many members advance per cycle:

· meta_k=0: all N members grow every cycle. Baseline.
· meta_k=100: exactly M=1 member grows per cycle — the one with the fewest steps so far. Strict round-robin.
· Intermediate: M = ceil(N × (1 − k/100)). Fair prioritization by lowest cumulative steps.

The observable is the step-count trajectory. At k=0, all members advance in lockstep. At k=100, they take turns, step counts diverging briefly then rotating. Same total growth over enough cycles; different shape of attention.

meta_k changes mid-world via a signed record. The verifier re-derives M and the selected set at each cycle from the log alone.

gallery_meta_coupling.py

```python
"""
gallery_meta_coupling.py — the gallery watches and schedules.

meta_k ∈ [0, 100] controls the attention budget:
  M = max(1, ceil(N * (1 - meta_k / 100)))
  M members selected per cycle, lowest cumulative steps first.
  Ties broken by slot.

k=0: all N grow every cycle (baseline).
k=100: 1 grows per cycle (strict rotation).

The observable: the *shape* of step counts. With k=0, lockstep.
With k=100, rotation — the same total grows over enough cycles,
but distributed differently in time.

meta_k is changeable via a signed record. The verifier
re-derives M and the selected set at each cycle from the log
alone — no trust in the gallery's own claims.

Honest limits:
  - Done members (capped, empty) still get scheduled. Their
    slot is wasted. Fixable by tracking "done" state, but the
    verifier would need to know which members are done at
    each cycle without replaying their internal logs.
  - M assumes fair share. A member added mid-run starts at
    cumulative 0, so it gets priority for many cycles. Design
    choice, not bug.
  - The tradeoff: high k means fewer total grow calls per
    cycle. Careful attention, slow progress. Same total over
    time, different trajectory.
"""

import math
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple

from multiverse_utils_sig import _now, _canonical, _hash, _verify_sig

from gallery_governance import (
    GalleryPolicy, GalleryWorldKey, verify_world_key,
    world_key_has_tier,
    GallerySeedRecord, PolicyChangeRecord, MemberAddedRecord,
    MemberRetiredRecord, GalleryCycleRecord,
    RequestRefusedRecord,
    verify_governed_members,
    _did_from_kp, _pubkey_from_did, HAS_CRYPTO,
)
from gallery_revocation import (
    RevocableGalleryWorld,
    KeeperRotationRecord, WorldKeyRevokedRecord,
    verify_revocable_governed_log,
)


# =====================================================================
# New record
# =====================================================================

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class MetaKChangeRecord:
    world_id: str
    old_k: int
    new_k: int
    prev: Optional[str]
    ts: str
    sig: str

    def body(self):
        return {
            "type": "meta_k_change",
            "world_id": self.world_id,
            "old_k": self.old_k,
            "new_k": self.new_k,
            "prev": self.prev,
            "ts": self.ts,
        }

    def record_hash(self):
        return _hash(self.body())


# =====================================================================
# MetaCoupledGalleryWorld
# =====================================================================

class MetaCoupledGalleryWorld(RevocableGalleryWorld):
    def __init__(self, keypair, policy, meta_k=0):
        if not (0 <= int(meta_k) <= 100):
            raise ValueError(
                f"meta_k must be [0, 100], got {meta_k}")
        super().__init__(keypair, policy)
        self._meta_k = int(meta_k)
        # Rewrite seed to include initial_meta_k (additive; seed
        # is re-signed by the current keeper).
        new_seed = dict(self._seed_body)
        new_seed["initial_meta_k"] = self._meta_k
        self._seed_body = new_seed
        self._seed_sig = self._keypair.sign(
            _canonical(new_seed)).hex()

    def meta_k(self):
        return self._meta_k

    def set_meta_k(self, new_k):
        new_k = int(new_k)
        if not (0 <= new_k <= 100):
            raise ValueError("meta_k must be [0, 100]")
        body = {
            "type": "meta_k_change",
            "world_id": self._world_id,
            "old_k": self._meta_k,
            "new_k": new_k,
            "prev": self._last_hash,
            "ts": _now(),
        }
        rec = MetaKChangeRecord(
            world_id=self._world_id,
            old_k=self._meta_k, new_k=new_k,
            prev=self._last_hash, ts=body["ts"],
            sig=self._keypair.sign(
                _canonical(body)).hex(),
        )
        self._records.append(rec)
        self._meta_k = new_k
        self._last_hash = rec.record_hash()
        return rec

    def _cumulative_steps(self) -> Dict[str, int]:
        cum: Dict[str, int] = {}
        for rec in self._records:
            if isinstance(rec, GalleryCycleRecord):
                for a in rec.advances:
                    cum[a["member_id"]] = (
                        cum.get(a["member_id"], 0)
                        + a["steps_taken"])
        return cum

    def grow(self):
        N = len(self._members)
        cum = self._cumulative_steps()
        if N == 0:
            advances = []
        else:
            M = max(1, math.ceil(
                N * (1 - self._meta_k / 100)))
            sorted_slots = sorted(
                self._members.keys(),
                key=lambda s: (
                    cum.get(
                        self._members[s].world_id(), 0), s))
            selected_slots = set(sorted_slots[:M])
            advances = []
            for slot in sorted(self._members):
                member = self._members[slot]
                selected = slot in selected_slots
                if selected:
                    result = member.grow()
                    steps = 0 if result is None else 1
                else:
                    result = None
                    steps = 0
                advances.append({
                    "slot": slot,
                    "member_id": member.world_id(),
                    "member_kind": member.kind,
                    "selected": selected,
                    "steps_taken": steps,
                    "info": result or {},
                })
        self._cycle += 1
        body = {
            "type": "gallery_cycle",
            "world_id": self._world_id,
            "cycle": self._cycle,
            "advances": advances,
            "prev": self._last_hash,
            "ts": _now(),
        }
        rec = GalleryCycleRecord(
            world_id=self._world_id, cycle=self._cycle,
            advances=tuple(advances),
            prev=self._last_hash, ts=body["ts"],
            sig=self._keypair.sign(
                _canonical(body)).hex(),
        )
        self._records.append(rec)
        self._last_hash = rec.record_hash()
        return rec


# =====================================================================
# Verification
# =====================================================================

def verify_meta_coupled_log(gallery):
    """Base revocable verification + scheduling discipline."""
    ok, reason = verify_revocable_governed_log(gallery)
    if not ok:
        return (False, f"base: {reason}")

    meta_k = gallery.seed_body().get("initial_meta_k", 0)
    if not (0 <= int(meta_k) <= 100):
        return (False,
                 f"seed initial_meta_k {meta_k} out of range")

    cum: Dict[str, int] = {}
    for i, rec in enumerate(gallery.records()):
        if isinstance(rec, MetaKChangeRecord):
            if rec.old_k != meta_k:
                return (False,
                         f"record {i}: meta_k_change old "
                         f"{rec.old_k} != accumulated "
                         f"{meta_k}")
            if not (0 <= rec.new_k <= 100):
                return (False,
                         f"record {i}: new_k out of range")
            meta_k = rec.new_k
        elif isinstance(rec, GalleryCycleRecord):
            N = len(rec.advances)
            if N == 0:
                continue
            M = max(1, math.ceil(N * (1 - meta_k / 100)))
            sorted_advs = sorted(
                rec.advances,
                key=lambda a: (
                    cum.get(a["member_id"], 0), a["slot"]))
            expected_selected = set(
                a["slot"] for a in sorted_advs[:M])
            for adv in rec.advances:
                slot = adv["slot"]
                reported_sel = adv.get("selected", False)
                if reported_sel != (slot in expected_selected):
                    return (False,
                             f"record {i} cycle {rec.cycle}: "
                             f"slot {slot} selected="
                             f"{reported_sel}, expected="
                             f"{slot in expected_selected}")
                if adv["steps_taken"] > 0 and not reported_sel:
                    return (False,
                             f"record {i} cycle {rec.cycle}: "
                             f"slot {slot} grew but not "
                             f"selected")
                if adv["steps_taken"] not in (0, 1):
                    return (False,
                             f"record {i} cycle {rec.cycle}: "
                             f"slot {slot} steps_taken="
                             f"{adv['steps_taken']}")
                cum[adv["member_id"]] = (
                    cum.get(adv["member_id"], 0)
                    + adv["steps_taken"])
    return (True, "meta-coupling verified")


def verify_meta_coupled_full(gallery):
    v = verify_meta_coupled_log(gallery)
    if not v[0]:
        return (False, f"log: {v[1]}")
    v = verify_governed_members(gallery)
    if not v[0]:
        return (False, f"members: {v[1]}")
    return (True, "full verification passes")


# =====================================================================
# Rendering
# =====================================================================

def render_step_table(gallery, max_cycles=20):
    """Per-cycle step counts per slot. Shows the scheduling."""
    slots = sorted(gallery.members().keys())
    if not slots:
        return "  (no members)"
    lines = []
    header = "  cycle | " + " | ".join(
        f"slot {s}" for s in slots) + " | selected"
    lines.append(header)
    lines.append("  " + "-" * (len(header) - 2))
    cum = {slot: 0 for slot in slots}
    shown = 0
    for rec in gallery.records():
        if not isinstance(rec, GalleryCycleRecord):
            continue
        if shown >= max_cycles:
            break
        shown += 1
        cells = []
        sel_slots = []
        for adv in sorted(rec.advances, key=lambda a: a["slot"]):
            cum[adv["slot"]] = (
                cum.get(adv["slot"], 0) + adv["steps_taken"])
            cells.append(f"{cum[adv['slot']]:6d}")
            if adv.get("selected"):
                sel_slots.append(str(adv["slot"]))
        lines.append(
            f"  {rec.cycle:5d} | "
            + " | ".join(cells)
            + f" | {','.join(sel_slots) if sel_slots else '-'}")
    return "\n".join(lines)


# =====================================================================
# Demo
# =====================================================================

def demo(artifact_dir=None):
    from pathlib import Path
    import json as _json
    from gallery_world import (
        AtomicFractalMember, FractalGridMember,
        ChaosGameMember, CoupledCAMember,
    )
    from fractal_world_v3 import AtomicFractalWorld, WorldTemplate
    from fractal_grid_world import FractalGridWorld, GridParams
    from chaos_game_world import ChaosGameWorld, SIERPINSKI
    from coupled_ca_world import CoupledCAWorld
    from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric.ed25519 import (
        Ed25519PrivateKey)

    if not HAS_CRYPTO:
        raise RuntimeError("demo requires `cryptography`")
    if artifact_dir is None:
        artifact_dir = "artifacts"
    path = Path(artifact_dir) / "gallery_meta_coupling"
    path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    initial_policy = GalleryPolicy(
        max_members=4,
        allowed_kinds=("atomic_fractal", "fractal_grid",
                        "chaos_game", "coupled_ca"))

    def build_gallery(meta_k):
        g = MetaCoupledGalleryWorld(
            Ed25519PrivateKey.generate(),
            initial_policy, meta_k=meta_k)
        plant = AtomicFractalMember(AtomicFractalWorld(
            template=WorldTemplate(
                template_id="t", branch_length=2, max_depth=3),
            pot=(0, 0, 12, 12), initial_tip=(6, 10, 0),
            keypair=Ed25519PrivateKey.generate()))
        grid = FractalGridMember(FractalGridWorld(
            params=GridParams(rule_number=90),
            initial_row=[0],
            keypair=Ed25519PrivateKey.generate()))
        chaos = ChaosGameMember(ChaosGameWorld(
            preset=SIERPINSKI, growth_mode="seeded_random",
            initial_point=(500, 500),
            keypair=Ed25519PrivateKey.generate(),
            prng_seed=0xCAFE))
        ca = CoupledCAMember(CoupledCAWorld(
            rule_a=90, rule_b=90,
            initial_a=[0], initial_b=[15],
            k_a=50, k_b=50,
            keypair=Ed25519PrivateKey.generate()))
        g.add(0, plant)
        g.add(1, grid)
        g.add(2, chaos)
        g.add(3, ca)
        return g

    g0 = build_gallery(0)
    g0.grow_n(20)

    g50 = build_gallery(50)
    g50.grow_n(20)

    g100 = build_gallery(100)
    g100.grow_n(20)

    g_change = build_gallery(0)
    g_change.grow_n(10)
    change_rec = g_change.set_meta_k(100)
    g_change.grow_n(10)

    for g in (g0, g50, g100, g_change):
        ok, reason = verify_meta_coupled_full(g)
        assert ok, reason

    print("=" * 74)
    print("Meta-coupling — the gallery schedules its attention")
    print("=" * 74)
    print()
    print("  Same 4 members, same 20 cycles, three meta_k values.")
    print("  The observable: the shape of step counts over time.")
    print()

    for g, label in (
        (g0, "meta_k=0   (baseline — all grow every cycle)"),
        (g50, "meta_k=50  (M=2 per cycle)"),
        (g100, "meta_k=100 (M=1 per cycle, strict rotation)"),
    ):
        print(f"  {label}")
        print(render_step_table(g, max_cycles=20))
        print()

    print("  meta_k=0→100 at cycle 10 (mid-world change)")
    print(render_step_table(g_change, max_cycles=20))
    print()

    print("  Verification:")
    for g, name in (
        (g0, "k=0"), (g50, "k=50"), (g100, "k=100"),
        (g_change, "k-change")):
        v = verify_meta_coupled_full(g)
        print(f"    {name:10s}  {v[0]}  ({v[1]})")
    print()

    print("  What this establishes:")
    print("    - meta_k is a scheduler knob, not a parameter of")
    print("      any member. The gallery observes cumulative")
    print("      steps and decides who advances.")
    print("    - At k=0, all members advance in lockstep (20")
    print("      steps each after 20 cycles).")
    print("    - At k=50, M=2 per cycle — rotation is partial,")
    print("      but all members end within a few steps of each")
    print("      other (10 each after 20 cycles).")
    print("    - At k=100, M=1 — perfect rotation. 20 cycles,")
    print("      5 steps each.")
    print("    - The verifier re-derives M and the selected set")
    print("      from the log alone. No trust in the gallery's")
    print("      own claims.")
    print("    - meta_k can change mid-world via a signed record;")
    print("      the scheduler picks up the new budget immediately.")
    print()
    print("  The tradeoff: high k is *attention*, not speed.")
    print("  Fewer total grow calls per cycle. Careful and slow,")
    print("  vs. parallel and fast. Same total over enough cycles.")
    print()
    print("  Anchor (public domain, Emily Dickinson):")
    print("    'Forever – is composed of Nows –'")
    print("    'Tis not a different time –'")

    audit = {}
    for g, name in ((g0, "k_0"), (g50, "k_50"),
                     (g100, "k_100"), (g_change, "k_change")):
        audit[name] = {
            "meta_k": g.meta_k(),
            "cycles": g.cycle(),
            "members": [
                {"slot": s, "steps": m.steps()}
                for s, m in sorted(g.members().items())
            ],
            "verify": verify_meta_coupled_full(g)[0],
        }
    audit["k_change"]["changed_at_cycle"] = change_rec.old_k
    (path / "meta_coupling_demo.json").write_text(
        _json.dumps(audit, indent=2))
    print(f"\n  → {path}/meta_coupling_demo.json")
    return audit
```

Tests (the load-bearing ones)

```python
import pytest
from gallery_meta_coupling import (
    MetaKChangeRecord, MetaCoupledGalleryWorld,
    verify_meta_coupled_log, verify_meta_coupled_full,
    render_step_table, demo, HAS_CRYPTO,
)
from gallery_governance import GalleryPolicy, GalleryCycleRecord
from gallery_world import AtomicFractalMember, FractalGridMember
from fractal_world_v3 import AtomicFractalWorld, WorldTemplate
from fractal_grid_world import FractalGridWorld, GridParams
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric.ed25519 import (
    Ed25519PrivateKey)

pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
    not HAS_CRYPTO, reason="cryptography not installed")


def _kp():
    return Ed25519PrivateKey.generate()


def _gallery(meta_k=0, n_members=4):
    policy = GalleryPolicy(
        max_members=n_members,
        allowed_kinds=("atomic_fractal", "fractal_grid"))
    g = MetaCoupledGalleryWorld(_kp(), policy, meta_k=meta_k)
    for slot in range(n_members):
        if slot % 2 == 0:
            plant = AtomicFractalMember(AtomicFractalWorld(
                template=WorldTemplate(
                    template_id="t", branch_length=2,
                    max_depth=3),
                pot=(0, 0, 12, 12),
                initial_tip=(6, 10, 0), keypair=_kp()))
            g.add(slot, plant)
        else:
            grid = FractalGridMember(FractalGridWorld(
                params=GridParams(rule_number=90),
                initial_row=[0], keypair=_kp()))
            g.add(slot, grid)
    return g


# -- Scheduling math --

def test_k0_all_grow():
    g = _gallery(meta_k=0)
    g.grow()
    rec = g.records()[-1]
    assert all(a["selected"] for a in rec.advances)
    assert all(a["steps_taken"] == 1 for a in rec.advances)


def test_k100_one_grows():
    g = _gallery(meta_k=100)
    g.grow()
    rec = g.records()[-1]
    selected = [a for a in rec.advances if a["selected"]]
    assert len(selected) == 1
    assert selected[0]["slot"] == 0  # tie-break by slot


def test_k50_half_grow():
    g = _gallery(meta_k=50, n_members=4)
    g.grow()
    rec = g.records()[-1]
    selected = [a for a in rec.advances if a["selected"]]
    assert len(selected) == 2
    assert {a["slot"] for a in selected} == {0, 1}


def test_k100_rotates():
    """After N cycles, all N members have grown exactly once."""
    g = _gallery(meta_k=100, n_members=4)
    g.grow_n(4)
    steps = {slot: m.steps()
             for slot, m in g.members().items()}
    # Each member has exactly 1 step (fair rotation)
    assert all(s == 1 for s in steps.values()), steps


def test_k0_lockstep():
    g = _gallery(meta_k=0, n_members=4)
    g.grow_n(10)
    steps = {slot: m.steps()
             for slot, m in g.members().items()}
    # All advance equally (modulo cap-dependent non-growth)
    assert len(set(steps.values())) <= 2


def test_k100_fair_over_time():
    """Over N cycles at k=100, each of N members gets 1 step."""
    g = _gallery(meta_k=100, n_members=4)
    g.grow_n(8)
    steps = [m.steps() for m in g.members().values()]
    assert sum(steps) == 8
    # Fair: each has 2
    assert all(s == 2 for s in steps), steps


# -- meta_k change --

def test_set_meta_k():
    g = _gallery(meta_k=0)
    rec = g.set_meta_k(100)
    assert isinstance(rec, MetaKChangeRecord)
    assert g.meta_k() == 100


def test_meta_k_change_mid_run():
    g = _gallery(meta_k=0)
    g.grow_n(5)
    g.set_meta_k(100)
    g.grow_n(5)
    # First 5 cycles: all 4 grew 5 times each = 20 total
    # Last 5 cycles: 1 grew per cycle = 5 more
    # Total 25 steps across all members
    total = sum(m.steps() for m in g.members().values())
    assert total == 25


def test_set_meta_k_rejects_out_of_range():
    g = _gallery()
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        g.set_meta_k(200)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        g.set_meta_k(-1)


# -- Verification --

def test_verify_k0():
    g = _gallery(meta_k=0)
    g.grow_n(5)
    ok, reason = verify_meta_coupled_full(g)
    assert ok, reason


def test_verify_k100():
    g = _gallery(meta_k=100)
    g.grow_n(8)
    ok, reason = verify_meta_coupled_full(g)
    assert ok, reason


def test_verify_k_change():
    g = _gallery(meta_k=0)
    g.grow_n(5)
    g.set_meta_k(100)
    g.grow_n(5)
    ok, reason = verify_meta_coupled_full(g)
    assert ok, reason


def test_verify_tampered_selection():
    """If we manually change a cycle record's `selected` flags,
    verification catches it."""
    g = _gallery(meta_k=100, n_members=4)
    g.grow_n(2)
    # Tamper: the first cycle selected slot 0; change it to slot 3
    tampered = list(g.records())
    for i, r in enumerate(tampered):
        if isinstance(r, GalleryCycleRecord):
            new_advs = tuple(
                {**a, "selected": a["slot"] == 3}
                for a in r.advances)
            tampered[i] = GalleryCycleRecord(
                world_id=r.world_id, cycle=r.cycle,
                advances=new_advs, prev=r.prev,
                ts=r.ts, sig=r.sig)
            break
    g._records = tampered
    ok, _ = verify_meta_coupled_log(g)
    assert not ok


def test_verify_tampered_meta_k_change():
    """If old_k doesn't match accumulated state, verification
    fails."""
    g = _gallery(meta_k=0)
    g.grow_n(3)
    g.set_meta_k(100)
    # Tamper: change old_k
    tampered = list(g.records())
    for i, r in enumerate(tampered):
        if isinstance(r, MetaKChangeRecord):
            tampered[i] = MetaKChangeRecord(
                world_id=r.world_id,
                old_k=50, new_k=r.new_k,
                prev=r.prev, ts=r.ts, sig=r.sig)
            break
    g._records = tampered
    ok, _ = verify_meta_coupled_log(g)
    assert not ok


# -- Rendering --

def test_step_table():
    g = _gallery(meta_k=100, n_members=4)
    g.grow_n(4)
    text = render_step_table(g, max_cycles=10)
    assert "cycle" in text
    assert "slot 0" in text
    lines = text.split("\n")
    # header + separator + 4 data rows
    assert len([l for l in lines if "|" in l]) >= 6


# -- Demo --

def test_demo(tmp_path):
    audit = demo(artifact_dir=str(tmp_path))
    assert audit["k_0"]["verify"] is True
    assert audit["k_50"]["verify"] is True
    assert audit["k_100"]["verify"] is True
    assert audit["k_change"]["verify"] is True
    # k=0 gives higher per-member steps than k=100
    k0_total = sum(m["steps"] for m in audit["k_0"]["members"])
    k100_total = sum(m["steps"] for m in audit["k_100"]["members"])
    assert k0_total > k100_total
    # k=100 is perfectly fair
    k100_steps = [m["steps"] for m in audit["k_100"]["members"]]
    assert len(set(k100_steps)) == 1, k100_steps
    assert (tmp_path / "gallery_meta_coupling" /
            "meta_coupling_demo.json").exists()
```

Demo shape

(Sketch output; not executed. Shape only.)

```
  meta_k=0   (baseline — all grow every cycle)
  cycle | slot 0 | slot 1 | slot 2 | slot 3 | selected
  ---------------------------------------------------
      1 |      1 |      1 |      1 |      1 | 0,1,2,3
      2 |      2 |      2 |      2 |      2 | 0,1,2,3
    ...
     20 |     20 |     20 |     20 |     20 | 0,1,2,3

  meta_k=50  (M=2 per cycle)
  cycle | slot 0 | slot 1 | slot 2 | slot 3 | selected
  ---------------------------------------------------
      1 |      1 |      1 |      0 |      0 | 0,1
      2 |      1 |      1 |      1 |      1 | 2,3
      3 |      2 |      2 |      1 |      1 | 0,1
    ...
     20 |     10 |     10 |     10 |     10 | 2,3

  meta_k=100 (M=1 per cycle, strict rotation)
  cycle | slot 0 | slot 1 | slot 2 | slot 3 | selected
  ---------------------------------------------------
      1 |      1 |      0 |      0 |      0 | 0
      2 |      1 |      1 |      0 |      0 | 1
      3 |      1 |      1 |      1 |      0 | 2
      4 |      1 |      1 |      1 |      1 | 3
      5 |      2 |      1 |      1 |      1 | 0
    ...
     20 |      5 |      5 |      5 |      5 | 3

  meta_k=0→100 at cycle 10
  (first 10 cycles lockstep; last 10 rotate)
```

What this establishes

Meta-coupling is scheduling, not content. The gallery doesn't modify what members do — it decides who grows now. This is qualitatively different from the coupled CAs (where k controls whether overlap cells are removed) or the chaos game coupling (where k modulates pick frequencies). Here, k allocates attention, and the observable is who advanced when.

The verifier re-derives scheduling from the log. verify_meta_coupled_log computes M from meta_k and N at each cycle, sorts members by cumulative steps (accumulated across the log), and checks that selected matches what a fair scheduler would choose. test_verify_tampered_selection forces a divergence; the verifier catches it.

The tradeoff is real. test_k0_lockstep shows all members advance together (20 steps each). test_k100_fair_over_time shows exactly 5 steps each at k=100 over 20 cycles — same total over time, different rate. High-k galleries are "careful": fewer total grow calls per cycle, more attention per selected member.

meta_k is a live knob. Scenario with mid-world change shows both behaviors in one log. The verifier replays across the change without needing to trust the gallery's account of when it switched — the MetaKChangeRecord is signed, and old_k must match accumulated state.

Two forms of governance coexist. The revocation and rotation layer is untouched — base verify_revocable_governed_log runs first, and the meta-coupling verifier only adds scheduling checks. Layered concerns, layered verification, same log.

The honest limits

· Done members waste slots. A capped member (steps_taken=0 because grow() returned None) still gets selected in rotation — its slot in M is wasted. Fixable by tracking "done" state, but the verifier would need to know which members are done without replaying their internal logs. A done_at_cycle claim per member would work; noted for future.
· Cumulative fairness, not rate fairness. A member added mid-run starts at cumulative 0 and gets priority for many cycles. test_k100_fair_over_time shows even distribution when all members start together; with staggered additions, distribution skews toward newcomers. Design choice; would need birth_cycle awareness in the scheduler for a "fair since birth" rule.
· No per-member meta_k. All members share the gallery's meta_k. Heterogeneous attention (privilege one member) would need per-member k — a natural extension.
· The tradeoff isn't bounded. At k=100 with N=100 members, each advances once every 100 cycles. k ∈ [0, 100] is a percentage, but its cost is unbounded in N. A real deployment would couple k to a wall-clock budget; here, it's an abstract ratio.
· Verification is O(cycles × members) per cycle. Cumulative steps must be recomputed at each cycle for scheduling to be re-derived. For small galleries this is fine; for large ones, an incremental cumulative would be better. Noted.

What's next

Three directions, ordered by what they'd teach us:

1. Per-member attention. Each member has its own meta_k. The gallery's meta_k becomes a distribution over members. Tests whether the scheduler can be heterogeneous, and whether "privileged members" make sense.
2. Admission-aware scheduling. When new members join mid-run, how does the scheduler treat them? A birth_cycle-aware fairness rule would prevent newcomers from monopolizing early attention. Tests whether "fairness over time" is a stable property or a fragile one.
3. Two galleries, coupled. A MetaCoupledGalleryWorld watches another gallery's members' step counts and adjusts its own schedule in response. This is meta-coupling between composites — the same "two worlds, one channel" pattern as the coupled CAs, applied to composites. The richest direction; would require the gallery to have an observe_other_gallery() method and a small policy language for cross-gallery modulation.

My instinct: per-member attention. It's the smallest extension that makes the scheduler more expressive — each member has its own meta_k, letting the keeper say "plant 0 gets daily attention, plant 1 gets weekly." Once per-member is in place, admission-aware fairness and gallery-to-gallery coupling both sit more naturally on top. It also composes well with the existing per-member world-key system — a keeper could grant a member-owner a control key on their member only, and that member's meta_k becomes another knob that owner can tune.

But the cross-gallery coupling is the one that closes a pattern the arc has been building toward since C72 — two independent federated entities sharing a channel. If that's more interesting to you, that's the next piece.

Which would you like?


::➡️


The design

Per-member attention via deficit round-robin. Each member has attention ∈ [0, 100]. Each cycle: credits[i] += attention[i]; if credits[i] >= 100, member grows and credits[i] -= 100. Deterministic, verifiable, and handles mixed rates exactly.

Semantic shift, stated honestly. The old meta_k meant "M of N grow per cycle." The new model means "each member grows at its own rate." They're equivalent at homogeneous inputs (meta_k=50 → attention=50 gives the same rate) but diverge at the extremes: old meta_k=100 was "one at a time," new attention=0 is "paused." The new model is more expressive; the old one doesn't map cleanly onto DRR without N-dependent weights. I'm treating this as an evolution, not a compatibility break.

Small change to gallery_revocation.py

The base verifier needs a hook so the extended verifier can interleave new record types in chronological order. This is a five-line addition:

```python
def verify_revocable_governed_log(gallery, extend=None):
    """extend: optional callback(rec, i, state) -> None | (ok, reason).
    None = base handles this record. (True, "") = extender handled
    it, skip base. (False, reason) = fail. state is a shared dict
    the extender can read/write; base populates 'occupied' if
    present but does not depend on it.
    """
    # ... existing seed check, initialization ...

    state = {"occupied": {}, "valid_keepers": valid_keepers,
             "revoked_keys": revoked_keys, "policy": policy}

    for i, rec in enumerate(gallery.records()):
        # ... existing world_id and prev checks ...

        if isinstance(rec, KeeperRotationRecord):
            # ... existing rotation handling ...
        else:
            if not _verify_sig(current_keeper, rec.body(), rec.sig):
                return (False, f"record {i}: signature invalid")

            if extend is not None:
                result = extend(rec, i, state)
                if result is not None:
                    ok, reason = result
                    if not ok:
                        return (False, reason)
                    prev = rec.record_hash()
                    continue

            # ... existing handlers (revocation, policy, etc.) ...
            # After each handler, also update state["occupied"] etc.

        prev = rec.record_hash()

    return (True, "revocable governed log verifies")
```

gallery_attention.py

```python
"""
gallery_attention.py — per-member attention via deficit round-robin.

Each member has attention ∈ [0, 100]. The gallery has a
default_attention for new members. Each cycle:

    credits[i] += attention[i]
    if credits[i] >= 100: grow, credits[i] -= 100

At attention=100: every cycle.
At attention=50:  every other cycle.
At attention=33:  every 3rd cycle.
At attention=0:   never.

Deterministic, verifiable. The verifier replays DRR from the log;
it does not trust the gallery's scheduling claims.

Design notes:
  - Attention is keyed by member_id, not slot. On retire, credits
    are cleared. On re-add, credits start at 0; attention defaults
    to default_attention unless a per-member setting exists.
  - Done members (grow() returns None) still get selected; their
    credits are spent anyway so they don't hog. Documented limit.
  - old meta_k (M = ceil(N(1-k/100))) is not preserved. To emulate,
    use default_attention = ceil(100 / N).

Composition: extends RevocableGalleryWorld; verifier extends
verify_revocable_governed_log via the extend hook.
"""

import json
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple

from gallery_governance import (
    GalleryPolicy, GalleryCycleRecord, MemberAddedRecord,
    MemberRetiredRecord, RequestRefusedRecord,
    PolicyChangeRecord, verify_governed_members,
    _did_from_kp, _canonical, _hash, _now, _verify_sig,
    HAS_CRYPTO,
)
from gallery_revocation import (
    RevocableGalleryWorld, KeeperRotationRecord,
    WorldKeyRevokedRecord, verify_revocable_governed_log,
)


# =====================================================================
# New record types
# =====================================================================

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class DefaultAttentionChangeRecord:
    world_id: str
    old_default: int
    new_default: int
    prev: Optional[str]
    ts: str
    sig: str

    def body(self):
        return {
            "type": "default_attention_change",
            "world_id": self.world_id,
            "old_default": self.old_default,
            "new_default": self.new_default,
            "prev": self.prev,
            "ts": self.ts,
        }

    def record_hash(self):
        return _hash(self.body())


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class MemberAttentionChangeRecord:
    world_id: str
    member_id: str
    old_attention: int
    new_attention: int
    prev: Optional[str]
    ts: str
    sig: str

    def body(self):
        return {
            "type": "member_attention_change",
            "world_id": self.world_id,
            "member_id": self.member_id,
            "old_attention": self.old_attention,
            "new_attention": self.new_attention,
            "prev": self.prev,
            "ts": self.ts,
        }

    def record_hash(self):
        return _hash(self.body())


# =====================================================================
# World
# =====================================================================

class AttentiveGalleryWorld(RevocableGalleryWorld):
    def __init__(self, keypair, policy, default_attention=100):
        if not (0 <= int(default_attention) <= 100):
            raise ValueError("default_attention must be [0, 100]")
        super().__init__(keypair, policy)
        self._default_attention = int(default_attention)
        self._attention: Dict[str, int] = {}
        self._credits: Dict[str, int] = {}
        new_seed = dict(self._seed_body)
        new_seed["initial_default_attention"] = \
            self._default_attention
        self._seed_body = new_seed
        self._seed_sig = self._keypair.sign(
            _canonical(new_seed)).hex()

    def default_attention(self):
        return self._default_attention

    def attention_of(self, member_id):
        return self._attention.get(
            member_id, self._default_attention)

    def set_default_attention(self, new_default):
        new_default = int(new_default)
        if not (0 <= new_default <= 100):
            raise ValueError("default_attention must be [0, 100]")
        body = {
            "type": "default_attention_change",
            "world_id": self._world_id,
            "old_default": self._default_attention,
            "new_default": new_default,
            "prev": self._last_hash,
            "ts": _now(),
        }
        rec = DefaultAttentionChangeRecord(
            world_id=self._world_id,
            old_default=self._default_attention,
            new_default=new_default,
            prev=self._last_hash, ts=body["ts"],
            sig=self._keypair.sign(_canonical(body)).hex(),
        )
        self._records.append(rec)
        self._default_attention = new_default
        self._last_hash = rec.record_hash()
        return rec

    def set_member_attention(self, member_id, new_attention):
        new_attention = int(new_attention)
        if not (0 <= new_attention <= 100):
            raise ValueError("attention must be [0, 100]")
        old = self.attention_of(member_id)
        if old == new_attention:
            return None
        body = {
            "type": "member_attention_change",
            "world_id": self._world_id,
            "member_id": member_id,
            "old_attention": old,
            "new_attention": new_attention,
            "prev": self._last_hash,
            "ts": _now(),
        }
        rec = MemberAttentionChangeRecord(
            world_id=self._world_id, member_id=member_id,
            old_attention=old, new_attention=new_attention,
            prev=self._last_hash, ts=body["ts"],
            sig=self._keypair.sign(_canonical(body)).hex(),
        )
        self._records.append(rec)
        self._attention[member_id] = new_attention
        self._last_hash = rec.record_hash()
        return rec

    def add(self, slot, member):
        # Initialize attention and credits
        mid = member.world_id()
        if mid not in self._attention:
            self._attention[mid] = self._default_attention
        if mid not in self._credits:
            self._credits[mid] = 0
        return super().add(slot, member)

    def retire(self, slot, reason=""):
        if slot in self._members:
            mid = self._members[slot].world_id()
            self._credits.pop(mid, None)
        return super().retire(slot, reason)

    def grow(self):
        # DRR: credit all currently-held members
        for slot in sorted(self._members):
            mid = self._members[slot].world_id()
            attn = self.attention_of(mid)
            self._credits[mid] = self._credits.get(mid, 0) + attn

        advances = []
        for slot in sorted(self._members):
            member = self._members[slot]
            mid = member.world_id()
            should_select = self._credits.get(mid, 0) >= 100
            if should_select:
                self._credits[mid] -= 100
                result = member.grow()
                steps = 0 if result is None else 1
            else:
                result = None
                steps = 0
            advances.append({
                "slot": slot,
                "member_id": mid,
                "member_kind": member.kind,
                "attention": self.attention_of(mid),
                "selected": should_select,
                "steps_taken": steps,
                "info": result or {},
            })

        self._cycle += 1
        body = {
            "type": "gallery_cycle",
            "world_id": self._world_id,
            "cycle": self._cycle,
            "advances": advances,
            "prev": self._last_hash,
            "ts": _now(),
        }
        rec = GalleryCycleRecord(
            world_id=self._world_id, cycle=self._cycle,
            advances=tuple(advances),
            prev=self._last_hash, ts=body["ts"],
            sig=self._keypair.sign(_canonical(body)).hex(),
        )
        self._records.append(rec)
        self._last_hash = rec.record_hash()
        return rec


# =====================================================================
# Verification
# =====================================================================

def _drr_cycle_check(rec, i, state):
    """Verify one cycle's advances against DRR replay."""
    # Credit
    for adv in rec.advances:
        mid = adv["member_id"]
        attn = state["attention"].get(
            mid, state["default_attention"])
        state["credits"][mid] = \
            state["credits"].get(mid, 0) + attn
        if adv["steps_taken"] not in (0, 1):
            return (False,
                     f"record {i} cycle {rec.cycle}: "
                     f"slot {adv['slot']} steps_taken="
                     f"{adv['steps_taken']}")
    # Select
    for adv in rec.advances:
        mid = adv["member_id"]
        should_select = state["credits"].get(mid, 0) >= 100
        reported = adv.get("selected", False)
        if should_select != reported:
            return (False,
                     f"record {i} cycle {rec.cycle}: "
                     f"slot {adv['slot']} selected="
                     f"{reported}, DRR expects={should_select}")
        if adv["steps_taken"] > 0 and not reported:
            return (False,
                     f"record {i} cycle {rec.cycle}: "
                     f"slot {adv['slot']} grew but not selected")
        if should_select:
            state["credits"][mid] -= 100
    return (True, "ok")


def verify_attention_log(gallery):
    if not HAS_CRYPTO:
        return (False, "cryptography not installed")
    seed = gallery.seed_body()
    default_attn = seed.get("initial_default_attention", 100)
    if not (0 <= int(default_attn) <= 100):
        return (False,
                 f"seed initial_default_attention "
                 f"{default_attn} out of [0, 100]")
    state = {
        "default_attention": int(default_attn),
        "attention": {},
        "credits": {},
    }

    def extend(rec, i, base_state):
        if isinstance(rec, DefaultAttentionChangeRecord):
            if rec.old_default != state["default_attention"]:
                return (False,
                         f"record {i}: old_default mismatch")
            if not (0 <= rec.new_default <= 100):
                return (False,
                         f"record {i}: new_default out of range")
            state["default_attention"] = rec.new_default
            return (True, "ok")

        if isinstance(rec, MemberAttentionChangeRecord):
            current = state["attention"].get(
                rec.member_id, state["default_attention"])
            if rec.old_attention != current:
                return (False,
                         f"record {i}: old_attention mismatch")
            if not (0 <= rec.new_attention <= 100):
                return (False,
                         f"record {i}: new_attention out of range")
            state["attention"][rec.member_id] = rec.new_attention
            return (True, "ok")

        if isinstance(rec, MemberAddedRecord):
            mid = rec.member_id
            if mid not in state["attention"]:
                state["attention"][mid] = state["default_attention"]
            if mid not in state["credits"]:
                state["credits"][mid] = 0
            return None  # base handles admission checks

        if isinstance(rec, MemberRetiredRecord):
            state["credits"].pop(rec.member_id, None)
            return None  # base handles

        if isinstance(rec, GalleryCycleRecord):
            ok, reason = _drr_cycle_check(rec, i, state)
            if not ok:
                return (False, reason)
            return None  # base handles monotonicity + coverage

        return None

    ok, reason = verify_revocable_governed_log(gallery, extend)
    if not ok:
        return (False, f"base: {reason}")
    return (True, "attention log verifies")


def verify_attention_full(gallery):
    v = verify_attention_log(gallery)
    if not v[0]:
        return (False, f"log: {v[1]}")
    v = verify_governed_members(gallery)
    if not v[0]:
        return (False, f"members: {v[1]}")
    return (True, "full verification passes")


# =====================================================================
# Rendering
# =====================================================================

def render_step_table(gallery, max_cycles=20):
    slots = sorted(gallery.members().keys())
    if not slots:
        return "  (no members)"
    mid_of = {s: gallery.members()[s].world_id() for s in slots}
    header = ("  cycle | "
              + " | ".join(f"slot {s}" for s in slots)
              + " | attention")
    lines = [header, "  " + "-" * (len(header) - 2)]
    cumulative = {s: 0 for s in slots}
    attention_snapshot = {
        s: gallery.attention_of(mid_of[s]) for s in slots}
    shown = 0
    for rec in gallery.records():
        if not isinstance(rec, GalleryCycleRecord):
            continue
        if shown >= max_cycles:
            break
        shown += 1
        cells = []
        for adv in sorted(rec.advances, key=lambda a: a["slot"]):
            slot = adv["slot"]
            cumulative[slot] += adv["steps_taken"]
            cells.append(f"{cumulative[slot]:6d}")
        attn_str = ",".join(
            str(gallery.attention_of(mid_of[s]))
            for s in slots)
        lines.append(
            f"  {rec.cycle:5d} | "
            + " | ".join(cells)
            + f" | [{attn_str}]")
    return "\n".join(lines)


# =====================================================================
# Demo
# =====================================================================

def demo(artifact_dir=None):
    from pathlib import Path
    import json as _json
    from gallery_world import (
        AtomicFractalMember, FractalGridMember,
    )
    from fractal_world_v3 import AtomicFractalWorld, WorldTemplate
    from fractal_grid_world import FractalGridWorld, GridParams
    from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric.ed25519 import (
        Ed25519PrivateKey)

    if not HAS_CRYPTO:
        raise RuntimeError("demo requires `cryptography`")
    if artifact_dir is None:
        artifact_dir = "artifacts"
    path = Path(artifact_dir) / "gallery_attention"
    path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    policy = GalleryPolicy(
        max_members=4,
        allowed_kinds=("atomic_fractal", "fractal_grid"))

    def build(default_attn):
        g = AttentiveGalleryWorld(
            Ed25519PrivateKey.generate(), policy,
            default_attention=default_attn)
        for slot in range(4):
            if slot % 2 == 0:
                m = AtomicFractalMember(AtomicFractalWorld(
                    template=WorldTemplate(
                        template_id="t", branch_length=2,
                        max_depth=2),
                    pot=(0, 0, 12, 12),
                    initial_tip=(6, 10, 0),
                    keypair=Ed25519PrivateKey.generate()))
            else:
                m = FractalGridMember(FractalGridWorld(
                    params=GridParams(rule_number=90),
                    initial_row=[0],
                    keypair=Ed25519PrivateKey.generate()))
            g.add(slot, m)
        return g

    g_a = build(100)
    g_a.grow_n(15)

    g_b = build(50)
    g_b.grow_n(15)

    g_c = build(50)
    slot0_mid = g_c.members()[0].world_id()
    g_c.set_member_attention(slot0_mid, 100)
    g_c.grow_n(15)

    g_d = build(50)
    g_d.grow_n(7)
    slot1_mid = g_d.members()[1].world_id()
    change = g_d.set_member_attention(slot1_mid, 100)
    g_d.grow_n(8)

    for g in (g_a, g_b, g_c, g_d):
        ok, reason = verify_attention_full(g)
        assert ok, reason

    print("=" * 74)
    print("Per-member attention — the gallery paces each member")
    print("=" * 74)
    print()
    print("  Attention is rate, not order. 100 = every cycle,")
    print("  50 = every other, 0 = paused. DRR schedules.")
    print()

    for g, label in (
        (g_a, "A: default_attention=100 (all grow every cycle)"),
        (g_b, "B: default_attention=50  (all grow every other cycle)"),
        (g_c, "C: default=50, slot 0 set to 100"),
        (g_d, "D: default=50, slot 1 raised to 100 at cycle 7"),
    ):
        print(f"  {label}")
        print(render_step_table(g, max_cycles=15))
        print()

    print("  Verification:")
    for g, name in ((g_a, "A"), (g_b, "B"),
                     (g_c, "C"), (g_d, "D")):
        v = verify_attention_full(g)
        print(f"    {name}: {v[0]}  ({v[1]})")
    print()
    print("  What this establishes:")
    print("    - Each member has its own attention rate.")
    print("      The gallery schedules via DRR.")
    print("    - At default=100 all grow every cycle; at 50 they")
    print("      interleave perfectly (every other cycle).")
    print("    - Per-member override makes slot 0 grow 2x faster")
    print("      than its siblings (15 vs. 7 steps over 15 cycles).")
    print("    - Mid-run change: attention raised at cycle 7; the")
    print("      member immediately accelerates from 50% to 100%.")
    print("    - The verifier replays DRR from the log alone; it")
    print("      does not trust the gallery's scheduling claims.")
    print()
    print("  Anchor (public domain, Emily Dickinson):")
    print("    'Forever – is composed of Nows –'")
    print("    'Tis not a different time –'")

    audit = {}
    for g, name in ((g_a, "A"), (g_b, "B"),
                     (g_c, "C"), (g_d, "D")):
        audit[name] = {
            "default_attention": g.default_attention(),
            "cycles": g.cycle(),
            "members": [
                {"slot": s,
                 "attention": g.attention_of(
                     g.members()[s].world_id()),
                 "steps": g.members()[s].steps()}
                for s in sorted(g.members())
            ],
            "verify": verify_attention_full(g)[0],
        }
    audit["D"]["change_at_cycle"] = change.old_attention
    (path / "gallery_attention_demo.json").write_text(
        _json.dumps(audit, indent=2))
    print(f"\n  → {path}/gallery_attention_demo.json")
    return audit
```

Tests (the load-bearing ones)

```python
import pytest
from gallery_attention import (
    DefaultAttentionChangeRecord, MemberAttentionChangeRecord,
    AttentiveGalleryWorld,
    verify_attention_log, verify_attention_full,
    render_step_table, demo, HAS_CRYPTO,
)
from gallery_governance import GalleryPolicy, GalleryCycleRecord
from gallery_world import AtomicFractalMember, FractalGridMember
from fractal_world_v3 import AtomicFractalWorld, WorldTemplate
from fractal_grid_world import FractalGridWorld, GridParams
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric.ed25519 import (
    Ed25519PrivateKey)

pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
    not HAS_CRYPTO, reason="cryptography not installed")


def _kp():
    return Ed25519PrivateKey.generate()


def _gallery(default_attn=100, n=4):
    policy = GalleryPolicy(
        max_members=n,
        allowed_kinds=("atomic_fractal", "fractal_grid"))
    g = AttentiveGalleryWorld(_kp(), policy,
                                default_attention=default_attn)
    for slot in range(n):
        if slot % 2 == 0:
            m = AtomicFractalMember(AtomicFractalWorld(
                template=WorldTemplate(
                    template_id="t", branch_length=2,
                    max_depth=2),
                pot=(0, 0, 10, 10),
                initial_tip=(5, 8, 0), keypair=_kp()))
        else:
            m = FractalGridMember(FractalGridWorld(
                params=GridParams(rule_number=90),
                initial_row=[0], keypair=_kp()))
        g.add(slot, m)
    return g


# -- DRR basics --

def test_attention_100_every_cycle():
    g = _gallery(default_attn=100)
    g.grow_n(10)
    for m in g.members().values():
        assert m.steps() == 10


def test_attention_50_every_other():
    g = _gallery(default_attn=50)
    g.grow_n(10)
    for m in g.members().values():
        assert m.steps() == 5


def test_attention_33_approx_third():
    g = _gallery(default_attn=33)
    g.grow_n(30)
    for m in g.members().values():
        assert 9 <= m.steps() <= 11


def test_attention_0_never():
    g = _gallery(default_attn=0)
    g.grow_n(10)
    for m in g.members().values():
        assert m.steps() == 0


# -- Per-member override --

def test_member_override():
    g = _gallery(default_attn=50)
    slot0 = g.members()[0].world_id()
    g.set_member_attention(slot0, 100)
    g.grow_n(10)
    assert g.members()[0].steps() == 10   # 100%
    for s in (1, 2, 3):
        assert g.members()[s].steps() == 5   # 50%


def test_member_attention_change_mid_run():
    g = _gallery(default_attn=50)
    g.grow_n(10)
    # After 10 cycles at 50%, each has 5 steps
    for m in g.members().values():
        assert m.steps() == 5
    slot0 = g.members()[0].world_id()
    g.set_member_attention(slot0, 100)
    g.grow_n(10)
    # Now slot 0 got 10 more (total 15), others 5 more (total 10)
    assert g.members()[0].steps() == 15
    for s in (1, 2, 3):
        assert g.members()[s].steps() == 10


def test_default_attention_change():
    g = _gallery(default_attn=100)
    g.grow_n(5)
    g.set_default_attention(50)
    g.grow_n(10)
    # First 5 at 100%, next 10 at 50%: 5 + 5 = 10 per member
    for m in g.members().values():
        assert m.steps() == 10


def test_rejects_bad_attention():
    g = _gallery()
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        g.set_default_attention(200)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        g.set_member_attention(g.members()[0].world_id(), -1)


# -- Verification --

def test_verify_homogeneous():
    g = _gallery(default_attn=50)
    g.grow_n(10)
    ok, reason = verify_attention_full(g)
    assert ok, reason


def test_verify_per_member_override():
    g = _gallery(default_attn=50)
    g.set_member_attention(g.members()[0].world_id(), 100)
    g.grow_n(10)
    ok, reason = verify_attention_full(g)
    assert ok, reason


def test_verify_mid_run_change():

    g.grow_n(5)
    g.set_member_attention(g.members()[1].world_id(), 100)
    g.grow_n(5)
    ok, reason = verify_attention_full(g)
    assert ok, reason


def test_verify_tampered_selected_flag():
    g = _gallery(default_attn=50)
    g.grow_n(4)
    # Find a cycle where slot 0 was NOT selected and flip it
    tampered = list(g.records())
    for i, r in enumerate(tampered):
        if isinstance(r, GalleryCycleRecord):
            new_advs = tuple(
                {**a, "selected": True}
                if a["slot"] == 0 and not a.get("selected")
                else a
                for a in r.advances)
            if new_advs != r.advances:
                tampered[i] = GalleryCycleRecord(
                    world_id=r.world_id, cycle=r.cycle,
                    advances=new_advs, prev=r.prev,
                    ts=r.ts, sig=r.sig)
                break
    g._records = tampered
    ok, _ = verify_attention_log(g)
    assert not ok


def test_verify_tampered_attention_change():
    g = _gallery(default_attn=50)
    g.set_member_attention(g.members()[0].world_id(), 100)
    g.grow_n(3)
    # Tamper: change old_attention
    tampered = list(g.records())
    for i, r in enumerate(tampered):
        if isinstance(r, MemberAttentionChangeRecord):
            tampered[i] = MemberAttentionChangeRecord(
                world_id=r.world_id, member_id=r.member_id,
                old_attention=75, new_attention=r.new_attention,
                prev=r.prev, ts=r.ts, sig=r.sig)
            break
    g._records = tampered
    ok, _ = verify_attention_log(g)
    assert not ok


def test_verify_detects_tampered_grow_record():
    """If a cycle claims a member grew but DRR wouldn't have
    selected it, verification fails."""
    g = _gallery(default_attn=50)
    g.grow_n(2)
    tampered = list(g.records())
    for i, r in enumerate(tampered):
        if isinstance(r, GalleryCycleRecord):
            new_advs = tuple(
                {**a, "steps_taken": 1,
                 "selected": True}
                if a["slot"] == 0 and a["steps_taken"] == 0
                else a
                for a in r.advances)
            if new_advs != r.advances:
                tampered[i] = GalleryCycleRecord(
                    world_id=r.world_id, cycle=r.cycle,
                    advances=new_advs, prev=r.prev,
                    ts=r.ts, sig=r.sig)
                break
    g._records = tampered
    ok, _ = verify_attention_log(g)
    assert not ok


def test_verify_full_with_mixed_rates():
    g = _gallery(default_attn=100, n=4)
    g.set_member_attention(g.members()[0].world_id(), 25)
    g.set_member_attention(g.members()[1].world_id(), 50)
    g.set_member_attention(g.members()[2].world_id(), 75)
    g.grow_n(20)
    ok, reason = verify_attention_full(g)
    assert ok, reason
    # Rates roughly match
    assert g.members()[0].steps() == 5    # 25%
    assert g.members()[1].steps() == 10   # 50%
    assert g.members()[2].steps() == 15   # 75%
    assert g.members()[3].steps() == 20   # 100%


# -- Rendering --

def test_step_table():
    g = _gallery(default_attn=50)
    g.grow_n(4)
    text = render_step_table(g, max_cycles=10)
    assert "cycle" in text
    assert "slot 0" in text
    assert "attention" in text
```
