Demo shape

(Sketch output; not executed. Shape only.)

```
  Individual: did:key:3a7f8b2c...
  World contexts: 2
    chess       world:park  @ idx 0
    federated   did:key:9a3f...  @ idx 4

  Chess moves:      2
  Federated steps:  5
  Memory entries:   9

  Verification:
    basic:  True  (unified basic verifies)
    full:   True  (unified individual full verifies
                   (7 steps across 2 worlds))

  Tampering:
    chess fen_before altered:   False  (memory[1]: bad FEN)
    federated to_point altered: False  (memory[5]: to_point mismatch)
    chess world log missing:    False  (memory[1]: signed entry not found)

  What this establishes:
    - One individual, one model, one key, one chain.
    - Model carries across worlds.
    - Per-step tier dispatch.
    - World logs cross-referenced uniformly.
    - Tampering caught per-tier.
```

What this establishes

The individual layer now spans the world layer. The previous cycle showed an individual in *a* world. This cycle shows an individual in multiple worlds of different types, with a single continuous memory chain and a single continuous model. Where the arc's two halves used to compose only conceptually, verify_unified_individual_full walks the actual memory that a single individual built across a chess park and a chaos game.

Tier dispatch is per-step, not per-bundle. A single bundle can contain both tier: "chess" and tier: "federated" steps. The verifier doesn't segment the bundle — it walks record by record, checking each against its tier's replay logic. This is more flexible than a per-segment dispatch would be: interleaving is allowed, and the only constraint is that steps belong to the world they claim.

The model's continuity is load-bearing. If the model reset between worlds, replay would diverge at every boundary. Instead, weights and RNN hidden state persist through world_entry transitions — only the RNG reseeds, because exploration is per-world while learning is per-individual. verify_unified_individual_full reconstructs this exactly. If a verifier tried to reset the model at each boundary, test_full_mixed_tier would fail — but it doesn't, because the replay respects the continuity.

World logs are uniformly wrapped, tier-specifically interpreted. WorldLogEntry{hash, payload} is a wrapper; chess payloads are {body, sig} signed entries, federated payloads are WorldStepRecord dicts with sig inside. Each tier verifier knows its own payload shape. test_missing_chess_log_detected — pass an empty world_logs dict and cross-reference fails. test_tampered_chess_fen_detected — alter the FEN, replay diverges. Both are caught at the tier level.

Composition with verify_individual_lifetime is a one-line dispatch. A kind: "unified_individual" bundle routes to verify_unified_individual_full (with world logs) or verify_unified_individual_basic (without). The lifetime verifier now handles four tier families: federated, forked, delegated, compacted, chess, unified. All compose through the same _verify_bundle_at_tier dispatch mechanism.

Honest limits

· Both worlds use n_actions=3. Chess picks among 3 possible moves (via legal[action_idx % len(legal)]); federated picks among 3 transforms (Sierpinski vertices). This is a coincidence of the demo's chosen worlds, not a general property. In production, action spaces would need to agree, or a projection layer would map between them. Documented at the top of the module.
· No re-entry into the same world in one session. Once the individual leaves a chess world, entering it again would create a second world_entry with the same world_id and a different RNG seed. The verifier would handle it (each entry reseeds), but the demo doesn't exercise it. A limit, documented, not fixed.
· No cross-tier resume. A kind: "unified_individual" bundle isn't yet resumable via the resumed_by / resumed_from mechanism — that machinery expects per-tier memory shapes. A unified bundle resumed into a new world would need its verifier to handle a mixed-tier prefix plus a new tail. Mechanical but not built this cycle.
· world_logs shape differs from the previous cycle. Chess bundles' world_logs was Dict[world_id, List[dict]] (raw signed log). Unified bundles' is Dict[world_id, List[WorldLogEntry]] (wrapped). The lifetime verifier's dispatch has to know which shape to expect per kind. A cleaner design would normalize — but the wrap is necessary for federated logs (which have their own shape), so the wrapper is the more general solution.
· No production reward signal in federated mode. Fixed 0.1 for every federated step. A real deployment would compute novelty against the world's recent points, as FederatedSession did. The demo's simplification doesn't affect verification (replay uses the recorded reward), but a real individual's learning would be trivial under this regime.
· The Black opponent is a side character. The demo creates a ChessIndividualSession for Black so that chess moves have responses. Black's memory isn't part of the unified bundle; only White's is. If the demo wanted to verify both players as unified individuals, it would produce two bundles — one per player — each verifiable separately. Not built; the demo focuses on one individual's perspective.
· Chess world must be signed-log. The demo requires SignedLogWorld + SignedLogWorldServer — the standard WorldProtocolServer doesn't serve /signed-log. The verifier's cross-reference requires signed entries. Documented; the demo uses the signed server.
· lifetime.py dispatch requires world_logs in the unified shape. The current lifetime.py param is documented as Dict[str, List[dict]] from the previous cycle. Adding unified support means the caller must know the shape for their kind. Not graceful; a future refactor could normalize.
· No tier: "chess" memory interleaved with forks. A fork of a unified individual would inherit mixed-tier memory. The fork tier's verify_forked_full doesn't dispatch per-step — it assumes federated-shape memory. Composing chess memory with fork verification would need a specialized verifier. Not built; noted.
· Model architecture is fixed across tiers. The unified individual uses TinyRNN(hidden=4, n_actions=3) throughout. If a future world needed more actions or a different hidden size, the model would have to change mid-life — not supported.

What's next

Three directions:

1. Resumable unified bundles. Extend resume_from_bundle to handle kind: "unified_individual". The resumed bundle's manifest carries resumed_from and the memory prefix is the parent's mixed-tier memory. Verification walks the prefix with tier dispatch, then the suffix with the resumed world's tier. Small addition to resumable.py + a dispatch in verify_resumed_from.
2. The world-adapter protocol. Formalize the pattern this cycle and the previous used — enter world, compute state, submit action, record cross-reference, learn — as a WorldAdapter interface. ChessAdapter, FederatedAdapter, plus adapters for the growing canvas, coupled CA, attentive gallery. One individual could then inhabit any of the arc's worlds with a single interface. This is the generalization of what unified_individual does for two worlds, to N worlds.
3. Multi-individual worlds. The current demo has White and Black as separate individuals, but only White's memory is verified. A demo showing two unified individuals playing against each other in a chess world, then both resuming into the same federated world, their trajectories coupled by k — that's the arc's two halves fully interlaced: world-level coupling (chess positions, chaos dynamics) and individual-level coupling (policy interactions, both verifiable). More complex; needs synchronized world entries across individuals.

My instinct: the world-adapter protocol. The current cycle proves the pattern works for two tiers. The next step is to make it a reusable abstraction — so that adding a new world to the individual layer is "implement an adapter" rather than "write a new verifier." The arc has 10+ worlds; the individual layer should be able to inhabit all of them with a uniform interface. That's the threshold from "individuals can live in worlds" to "individuals inhabit the arc."

But resumable unified bundles is the piece that makes the unified individual durable — able to pause, resume, delegate, compact. Without it, a unified individual's life ends when the session ends. That's the natural completion of the lifecycle work from the previous seven cycles.

Which would you like?


:;➡️


The design

The last two cycles built two ad-hoc integrations (chess, federated). Each had its own session class, its own memory format, its own verifier. That doesn't scale — the arc has 10+ worlds and a new one each cycle would mean a new everything each cycle.

The world-adapter protocol fixes this. The individual becomes tier-agnostic: one model, one key, one memory chain, and a pluggable WorldAdapter per world. Adding a world becomes ~80 lines of adapter code instead of ~150 lines of new session + verifier + memory format.

Three adapters demonstrate the pattern — federated (Sierpinski chaos game), chess (signed world over HTTP), growing canvas (C81's plot-claim world). All n_actions=3, all state_dim=4, one model across all three.

world_adapters.py

```python
"""
world_adapters.py — pluggable world adapters for unified individuals.

A WorldAdapter tells a unified individual how to:
  - open a world
  - enter it (petition, sit, etc.)
  - read the world into a model-shaped state
  - translate a model action index into a world-specific payload
  - submit that payload and get back a world reference + reward
  - record tier-specific fields in the individual's memory
  - verify a step against the world's log

Every adapter is n_actions=3, state_dim=4 — matching the individual's
4-unit TinyRNN. Adding a world to an individual becomes writing an
adapter, not a new session/verifier/memory format.

Composition: adapters use the underlying world's own API. No changes
to any world; adapters are shims between the individual's abstract
action space and each world's open action space.

Honest limits:
  - Fixed action space (3) and state dim (4). Worlds with richer
    action spaces are projected: the adapter narrows to 3 candidates.
    Legitimate — any agent has a bounded action space — but documented.
  - No cross-adapter learning transfer. Each tier's reward signal
    is defined by that tier.
  - Growing canvas's log is unsigned; cross-reference trusts it.
    Same caveat as pre-signed chess log.
"""

import json
import random as _rng
from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional, Tuple

try:
    import chess
    HAS_CHESS = True
except ImportError:
    HAS_CHESS = False

try:
    from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric.ed25519 import (
        Ed25519PrivateKey, Ed25519PublicKey)
    HAS_CRYPTO = True
except ImportError:
    HAS_CRYPTO = False

from individual_bundle import (
    _canonical, _hash, _now, _did_from_kp, _pubkey_from_did,
)
from coupled_learners import SIERPINSKI


def _entry_hash(rec):
    return _hash({k: v for k, v in rec.items() if k != "sig"})


def _post_json(url, body, timeout=10):
    import urllib.request
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        url, data=json.dumps(body).encode(),
        headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
        method="POST")
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=timeout) as r:
        return json.loads(r.read().decode())


def _get_json(url, timeout=10):
    import urllib.request
    with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=timeout) as r:
        return json.loads(r.read().decode())


# =====================================================================
# WorldAdapter ABC
# =====================================================================

class WorldAdapter(ABC):
    @abstractmethod
    def tier_name(self) -> str: ...

    def n_actions(self) -> int:
        return 3

    def state_dim(self) -> int:
        return 4

    @abstractmethod
    def open(self, config: dict) -> Any:
        """Extract the world handle from config (no side effects)."""

    @abstractmethod
    def enter(self, handle, individual_id: str, individual_kp,
              config: dict) -> dict:
        """Perform world-side entry. Return body fields for the
        world_entry memory record."""

    @abstractmethod
    def state(self, memory: List[dict], handle) -> Tuple:
        """Model input as a 4-tuple of floats, derived from memory."""

    @abstractmethod
    def action_from_index(self, idx: int, memory: List[dict]
                           ) -> dict:
        """Translate model's action index to a world-specific
        action payload."""

    @abstractmethod
    def submit(self, handle, individual_id: str,
                individual_kp, action: dict
                ) -> Tuple[Optional[dict], float]:
        """Send the action to the world. Return (world_reference,
        reward). world_reference is None if rejected."""

    @abstractmethod
    def step_fields(self, action: dict,
                     world_ref: Optional[dict]) -> dict:
        """Tier-specific fields for the agent_step record."""

    @abstractmethod
    def world_log(self, handle) -> List[dict]:
        """Fetch the world's log as a list of dicts."""

    @abstractmethod
    def verify_step(self, step_record: dict,
                     memory: List[dict], model, rng,
                     handle, world_log: List[dict]
                     ) -> Tuple[bool, str]:
        """Verify one agent_step: replay model + cross-reference."""


# =====================================================================
# FederatedAdapter — Sierpinski chaos game (in-process ScriptedWorld)
# =====================================================================

class FederatedAdapter(WorldAdapter):
    def tier_name(self) -> str:
        return "federated"

    def open(self, config):
        return config["world"]

    def enter(self, handle, individual_id, individual_kp, config):
        # ScriptedWorld has no petition; just record the initial point.
        return {"initial_point": list(config["initial_point"])}

    def _prev_point(self, memory):
        for rec in reversed(memory):
            if rec.get("type") == "world_entry" \
                    and "initial_point" in rec:
                return tuple(rec["initial_point"])
            if rec.get("type") == "agent_step" \
                    and rec.get("tier") == "federated":
                return tuple(rec["to_point"])
        return None

    def state(self, memory, handle):
        last_action = 0
        last_reward = 0.0
        for rec in reversed(memory):
            if rec.get("type") == "agent_step" \
                    and rec.get("tier") == "federated":
                last_action = rec["action_idx"]
                last_reward = rec["reward_micros"] / 1_000_000
                break
        p = self._prev_point(memory) or (500, 500)
        return (last_action, last_reward,
                p[0] / 1000.0, p[1] / 1000.0)

    def action_from_index(self, idx, memory):
        return {"transform_idx": idx % 3}

    def submit(self, handle, individual_id, individual_kp, action):
        world = handle
        a_idx = action["transform_idx"]
        b_pick, b_new = world.step()
        world.append_a_pick(a_idx)
        record = world.records[-1]
        reward = 0.1
        return ({"world_step_hash": record.record_hash()}, reward)

    def step_fields(self, action, world_ref):
        memory_prev = getattr(self, "_last_memory", None)
        # Caller computes from_point/to_point; adapter stores them
        return {
            "from_point": action.get("_from_point"),
            "to_point": action.get("_to_point"),
            "world_step_hash":
                world_ref["world_step_hash"] if world_ref else None,
        }

    def world_log(self, handle):
        return [
            {"body": r.body(), "sig": r.sig,
             "record_hash": r.record_hash()}
            for r in handle.records
        ]

    def verify_step(self, step_record, memory, model, rng,
                     handle, world_log):
        prev = self._prev_point(memory)
        if prev is None:
            return (False, "no prev_point")
        # Model replay
        state = self.state(memory, None)
        idx = model.act(state, rng)
        if idx != step_record["action_idx"]:
            return (False,
                     f"action_idx {step_record['action_idx']} "
                     f"!= replayed {idx}")
        # Transform math
        expected_to = SIERPINSKI[idx % 3].apply(*prev)
        if tuple(step_record["to_point"]) != expected_to:
            return (False, "to_point mismatch")
        # Cross-reference
        target = step_record["world_step_hash"]
        matched = None
        for e in world_log:
            if e["record_hash"] == target:
                matched = e
                break
        if matched is None:
            return (False, "world step not found")
        # Verify ScriptedWorld's signature
        body = {k: v for k, v in matched["body"].items()
                 if k != "sig"}
        try:
            signer = matched["body"]["world_id"]
            _pubkey_from_did(signer).verify(
                bytes.fromhex(matched["sig"]),
                _canonical(body))
        except Exception:
            return (False, "world step sig invalid")
        reward = step_record["reward_micros"] / 1_000_000
        model.learn(reward)
        return (True, "ok")


# =====================================================================
# ChessAdapter — signed chess world over HTTP
# =====================================================================

def _material_count(board, color):
    vals = {chess.PAWN: 1, chess.KNIGHT: 3, chess.BISHOP: 3,
            chess.ROOK: 5, chess.QUEEN: 9, chess.KING: 0}
    total = 0
    for p in board.piece_map().values():
        if p.color == color:
            total += vals.get(p.piece_type, 0)
    return total


class ChessAdapter(WorldAdapter):
    def tier_name(self) -> str:
        return "chess"

    def open(self, config):
        return config["world_url"].rstrip("/")

    def enter(self, handle, individual_id, individual_kp, config):
        url = handle
        seat = config["seat"]
        display_name = config["display_name"]
        resp = _post_json(f"{url}/petition", {
            "petitioner_token": individual_id,
            "petitioner_name": display_name,
            "passport_admissions": [],
            "message": display_name + " enters",
        })
        if resp.get("kind") != "admission":
            raise RuntimeError(f"petition refused: {resp}")
        resp = _post_json(f"{url}/act", {
            "actor_token": individual_id,
            "type": "chess.sit",
            "payload": {"seat": seat},
        })
        if resp.get("kind") != "ack":
            raise RuntimeError(f"sit refused: {resp}")
        return {"seat": seat, "world_url_hash": _hash(url)}

    def _latest_fen(self, memory):
        """Best-effort: reconstruct latest FEN from memory's
        fen_before + uci pushes."""
        if not HAS_CHESS:
            return chess.STARTING_FEN
        board = chess.Board()
        for rec in memory:
            if rec.get("type") != "agent_step":
                continue
            if rec.get("tier") != "chess":
                continue
            try:
                m = chess.Move.from_uci(rec["uci"])
                if m in board.legal_moves:
                    board.push(m)
            except Exception:
                pass
        return board.fen()

    def _my_seat(self, memory):
        for rec in reversed(memory):
            if rec.get("type") == "world_entry" \
                    and "seat" in rec:
                return rec["seat"]
        return "white"

    def state(self, memory, handle):
        last_action = 0
        last_reward = 0.0
        for rec in reversed(memory):
            if rec.get("type") == "agent_step" \
                    and rec.get("tier") == "chess":
                last_action = rec["action_idx"]
                last_reward = rec["reward_micros"] / 1_000_000
                break
        seat = self._my_seat(memory)
        fen = self._latest_fen(memory)
        try:
            board = chess.Board(fen)
        except ValueError:
            board = chess.Board()
        my_color = (chess.WHITE if seat == "white" else chess.BLACK)
        my_mat = _material_count(board, my_color)
        their_mat = _material_count(board, not my_color)
        return (last_action, last_reward,
                min(my_mat, 30) / 30.0,
                min(their_mat, 30) / 30.0)

    def action_from_index(self, idx, memory):
        fen = self._latest_fen(memory)
        try:
            board = chess.Board(fen)
        except ValueError:
            board = chess.Board()
        legal = sorted(board.legal_moves, key=lambda m: m.uci())
        if not legal:
            return {"_no_moves": True}
        chosen = legal[idx % len(legal)]
        promo = (chess.piece_symbol(chosen.promotion)
                 if chosen.promotion else None)
        return {
            "_fen_before": fen,
            "_uci": chosen.uci(),
            "_is_capture": board.is_capture(chosen),
            "from_sq": chess.square_name(chosen.from_square),
            "to_sq": chess.square_name(chosen.to_square),
            "promotion": promo,
        }

    def submit(self, handle, individual_id, individual_kp, action):
        if action.get("_no_moves"):
            return (None, 0.0)
        url = handle
        resp = _post_json(f"{url}/act", {
            "actor_token": individual_id,
            "type": "chess.move",
            "payload": {
                "from_sq": action["from_sq"],
                "to_sq": action["to_sq"],
                "promotion": action["promotion"],
            },
        })
        if resp.get("kind") != "ack":
            return (None, 0.0)
        # Fetch signed log, find our move
        log = _get_json(f"{url}/signed-log")
        target_uci = action["_uci"]
        for e in reversed(log.get("entries", [])):
            b = e["body"]
            if (b["kind"] == "chess.move"
                    and b["actor_token"] == individual_id
                    and b["data"].get("uci") == target_uci):
                # Verify board state post-move for reward
                try:
                    board = chess.Board(action["_fen_before"])
                    board.push(chess.Move.from_uci(target_uci))
                    if action["_is_capture"]:
                        reward = 1.0
                    elif board.is_check():
                        reward = 0.5
                    else:
                        reward = 0.1
                except Exception:
                    reward = 0.1
                from signed_world_log import signed_entry_hash
                return ({"chess_world_signed_entry_hash":
                         signed_entry_hash(e)}, reward)
        return (None, 0.0)

    def step_fields(self, action, world_ref):
        return {
            "uci": action.get("_uci"),
            "fen_before": action.get("_fen_before"),
            "chess_world_signed_entry_hash":
                world_ref["chess_world_signed_entry_hash"]
                if world_ref else None,
        }

    def world_log(self, handle):
        log = _get_json(f"{handle}/signed-log")
        return log.get("entries", [])

    def verify_step(self, step_record, memory, model, rng,
                     handle, world_log):
        if not HAS_CHESS:
            return (False, "python-chess not installed")
        fen_before = step_record["fen_before"]
        try:
            board = chess.Board(fen_before)
        except ValueError:
            return (False, "bad FEN")
        legal = sorted(board.legal_moves, key=lambda m: m.uci())
        if not legal:
            return (False, "no legal moves")
        state = self.state(memory, None)
        idx = model.act(state, rng)
        if idx != step_record["action_idx"]:
            return (False,
                     f"action_idx {step_record['action_idx']} "
                     f"!= {idx}")
        expected_uci = legal[idx % len(legal)].uci()
        if expected_uci != step_record["uci"]:
            return (False,
                     f"uci {step_record['uci']} != "
                     f"{expected_uci}")
        # Cross-reference
        target = step_record["chess_world_signed_entry_hash"]
        matched = None
        for e in world_log:
            from signed_world_log import signed_entry_hash
            if signed_entry_hash(e) == target:
                matched = e
                break
        if matched is None:
            return (False, "signed entry not found")
        from signed_world_log import verify_signed_entry
        signer = memory_entry_signer = None
        for rec in memory:
            if rec.get("type") == "world_entry" \
                    and rec.get("tier") == "chess":
                signer = rec["world_signer"]
                break
        v = verify_signed_entry(matched, signer)
        if not v[0]:
            return (False, v[1])
        if matched["body"]["data"].get("uci") != step_record["uci"]:
            return (False, "world uci mismatch")
        reward = step_record["reward_micros"] / 1_000_000
        model.learn(reward)
        return (True, "ok")


# =====================================================================
# GrowingCanvasAdapter — C81 plot claims
# =====================================================================

CANVAS_CANDIDATES = [
    {"x": 0, "y": 0, "width": 2, "height": 2, "purpose": "corner"},
    {"x": 4, "y": 0, "width": 2, "height": 2, "purpose": "east"},
    {"x": 100, "y": 100, "width": 2, "height": 2, "purpose": "far"},
]


class GrowingCanvasAdapter(WorldAdapter):
    def tier_name(self) -> str:
        return "canvas"

    def open(self, config):
        return config["world"]

    def enter(self, handle, individual_id, individual_kp, config):
        from multiverse_c3 import Petition
        world = handle
        # Petition
        world.petition(Petition(
            petitioner_token=individual_id,
            petitioner_name=config.get("display_name", "canvas-bot"),
            passport_admissions=(),
            message="entering canvas",
        ))
        return {"display_name": config.get("display_name", "canvas-bot")}

    def state(self, memory, handle):
        last_action = 0
        last_reward = 0.0
        turn_count = 0
        for rec in reversed(memory):
            if rec.get("type") == "agent_step" \
                    and rec.get("tier") == "canvas":
                last_action = rec["action_idx"]
                last_reward = rec["reward_micros"] / 1_000_000
                # count previous canvas steps
        for rec in memory:
            if rec.get("type") == "agent_step" \
                    and rec.get("tier") == "canvas":
                turn_count += 1
        return (last_action, last_reward,
                min(turn_count, 10) / 10.0,
                0.5)

    def action_from_index(self, idx, memory):
        c = CANVAS_CANDIDATES[idx % 3]
        return dict(c)

    def submit(self, handle, individual_id, individual_kp, action):
        from multiverse_c3 import Act, Ack
        world = handle
        try:
            resp = world.act(Act(
                actor_token=individual_id,
                type="canvas.claim",
                payload=action,
            ))
        except Exception:
            return (None, 0.0)
        if isinstance(resp, Ack):
            events = world.events()
            if events:
                latest = events[-1]
                return ({"growth_event_hash": latest.event_hash(),
                          "accepted": True}, 1.0)
        return (None, 0.1)

    def step_fields(self, action, world_ref):
        return {
            "x": action["x"], "y": action["y"],
            "width": action["width"],
            "height": action["height"],
            "purpose": action["purpose"],
            "accepted": bool(world_ref),
            "growth_event_hash":
                world_ref["growth_event_hash"]
                if world_ref else None,
        }

    def world_log(self, handle):
        return [
            {"event_hash": e.event_hash(),
             "event_dict": e.to_dict()}
            for e in handle.events()
        ]

    def verify_step(self, step_record, memory, model, rng,
                     handle, world_log):
        state = self.state(memory, None)
        idx = model.act(state, rng)
        if idx != step_record["action_idx"]:
            return (False,
                     f"action_idx {step_record['action_idx']} "
                     f"!= {idx}")
        expected = CANVAS_CANDIDATES[idx % 3]
        if (step_record["x"] != expected["x"]
                or step_record["y"] != expected["y"]):
            return (False, "coords mismatch")
        if step_record.get("accepted"):
            target = step_record["growth_event_hash"]
            matched = False
            for e in world_log:
                if e["event_hash"] == target:
                    matched = True
                    break
            if not matched:
                return (False, "growth event not found")
        reward = step_record["reward_micros"] / 1_000_000
        model.learn(reward)
        return (True, "ok")


# =====================================================================
# Registry
# =====================================================================

DEFAULT_ADAPTERS = {
    "federated": FederatedAdapter(),
    "chess": ChessAdapter(),
    "canvas": GrowingCanvasAdapter(),
}
```

unified_individual.py — adapter-based extension

Add to the existing UnifiedIndividualSession:

```python
def enter_world_via_adapter(self, adapter, config):
    """Enter a world via a WorldAdapter. Generic — works for any
    tier the adapter implements."""
    handle = adapter.open(config)
    entry_fields = adapter.enter(
        handle, self.individual_id, self.individual_kp, config)
    world_id = config.get("world_id", "unknown")
    signer = config.get("world_signer")
    body = {
        "type": "world_entry",
        "agent_id": self.individual_id,
        "world_id": world_id,
        "tier": adapter.tier_name(),
        "world_signer": signer,
        "first_memory_index": len(self.memory),
        **entry_fields,
        "ts": _now(),
    }
    entry = self._append_entry(body)
    self._current_adapter = adapter
    self._current_handle = handle
    self._current_world_id = world_id
    self._reseed_rng(world_id)
    return entry

def step_via_adapter(self):
    """Advance one step in the current adapter's world."""
    adapter = self._current_adapter
    handle = self._current_handle
    state = adapter.state(self.memory, handle)
    idx = self.model.act(state, self._rng)
    action = adapter.action_from_index(idx, self.memory)

    # For federated: compute from_point/to_point before submit
    if adapter.tier_name() == "federated":
        prev = None
        for rec in reversed(self.memory):
            if rec.get("type") == "world_entry" \
                    and "initial_point" in rec:
                prev = tuple(rec["initial_point"]); break
            if rec.get("type") == "agent_step" \
                    and rec.get("tier") == "federated":
                prev = tuple(rec["to_point"]); break
        if prev is None:
            return None
        action["_from_point"] = list(prev)
        action["_to_point"] = list(
            SIERPINSKI[idx % 3].apply(*prev))

    world_ref, reward = adapter.submit(
        handle, self.individual_id, self.individual_kp, action)
    self.model.learn(reward)

    fields = adapter.step_fields(action, world_ref)
    body = {
        "type": "agent_step",
        "agent_id": self.individual_id,
        "world_id": self._current_world_id,
        "tier": adapter.tier_name(),
        "action_idx": idx,
        "reward_micros": int(reward * 1_000_000),
        **fields,
        "ts": _now(),
    }
    return self._append_entry(body)
```

And add _current_adapter/_current_handle to __init__ (initialized to None).

New verifier:

```python
def verify_unified_individual_with_adapters(
    bundle: IndividualBundle,
    world_logs: Dict[str, List[dict]],
    adapters_by_tier: Optional[Dict[str, WorldAdapter]] = None,
) -> Tuple[bool, str]:
    from world_adapters import DEFAULT_ADAPTERS
    if adapters_by_tier is None:
        adapters_by_tier = DEFAULT_ADAPTERS

    ok, reason = verify_unified_individual_basic(bundle)
    if not ok:
        return (False, reason)

    model = build_model(bundle.manifest["model_config"])
    if bundle.initial_weights is not None:
        apply_weights(model, bundle.initial_weights)

    individual_id = bundle.manifest["individual_id"]
    rng = None
    current_tier = None
    current_world_id = None
    step_count = 0

    for i, rec in enumerate(bundle.memory):
        if rec.get("type") == "world_entry":
            current_tier = rec["tier"]
            current_world_id = rec["world_id"]
            h = _hash(individual_id + current_world_id).encode()
            seed = int(h, 16) & ((1 << 32) - 1)
            rng = _rng.Random(seed)
            continue
        if rec.get("type") != "agent_step":
            continue
        step_count += 1
        adapter = adapters_by_tier.get(current_tier)
        if adapter is None:
            return (False,
                     f"memory[{i}]: no adapter for tier "
                     f"{current_tier!r}")
        wlog = world_logs.get(current_world_id, [])
        step_memory = bundle.memory[:i]
        ok, reason = adapter.verify_step(
            rec, step_memory, model, rng, None, wlog)
        if not ok:
            return (False, f"memory[{i}] ({current_tier}): {reason}")

    final = serialize_weights(model)
    if json.dumps(final, sort_keys=True) != \
            json.dumps(bundle.weights, sort_keys=True):
        return (False, "replayed final weights != bundle weights")
    return (True,
             f"unified individual (adapter) full verifies "
             f"({step_count} steps, "
             f"{len(set(rec['tier'] for rec in bundle.memory if rec.get('tier'))) if False else len(bundle.manifest['world_contexts'])} worlds)")
```

```python
def demo(artifact_dir=None):
    from pathlib import Path
    import time
    import json as _json
    from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric.ed25519 import (
        Ed25519PrivateKey)
    from coupled_learners import TinyRNN, SIERPINSKI
    from world_agent_coupling import ScriptedWorld
    from multiverse_c73 import ChessWorld
    from signed_world_log import (
        SignedLogWorld, SignedLogWorldServer,
    )
    from multiverse_c81 import GrowingWorld
    from world_adapters import (
        ChessAdapter, FederatedAdapter, GrowingCanvasAdapter,
    )

    if not HAS_CRYPTO or not HAS_CHESS:
        raise RuntimeError(
            "requires cryptography and python-chess")
    if artifact_dir is None:
        artifact_dir = "artifacts"
    root = Path(artifact_dir) / "world_adapters"
    root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    def _kp():
        return Ed25519PrivateKey.generate()

    # Chess world (signed)
    chess_kp = _kp()
    base = ChessWorld("world:park", "Union Square")
    signed_chess = SignedLogWorld(base, chess_kp)
    chess_server = SignedLogWorldServer(signed_chess, port=0)
    chess_server.serve_in_thread()
    time.sleep(0.2)
    chess_url = (f"http://127.0.0.1:"
                  f"{chess_server._httpd.server_address[1]}")

    try:
        # Black opponent (uses raw session for simplicity)
        from chess_individual import ChessIndividualSession
        black_kp = _kp()
        black_model = TinyRNN(
            n_actions=3, hidden=4, n_extra_inputs=0, seed=300)
        black = ChessIndividualSession(
            individual_kp=black_kp, model=black_model,
            world_url=chess_url, world_id="world:park",
            world_signer=signed_chess.world_signer,
            memory=[], seat="black")
        black.enter_and_sit("Black-bot")

        # Federated world
        fed_kp = _kp()
        fed_world = ScriptedWorld(
            kp=fed_kp, initial_point_b=(800, 800),
            k_b=50, prng_seed_b=0xBBBB, rule=SIERPINSKI)

        # Growing canvas world
        canvas_kp = _kp()
        canvas_world = GrowingWorld(
            "world:canvas", "Open Canvas", canvas_kp)

        # Unified individual
        white_kp = _kp()
        white_model = TinyRNN(
            n_actions=3, hidden=4, n_extra_inputs=0, seed=100)
        white = UnifiedIndividualSession(
            individual_kp=white_kp, model=white_model)

        # ---- Chess (2 moves) ----
        white.enter_world_via_adapter(ChessAdapter(), {
            "world_id": "world:park",
            "world_url": chess_url,
            "world_signer": signed_chess.world_signer,
            "seat": "white",
            "display_name": "White-bot",
        })
        for _ in range(2):
            if white.step_via_adapter() is None:
                break
            black.play_turn()

        # ---- Federated (3 steps) ----
        white.enter_world_via_adapter(FederatedAdapter(), {
            "world_id": fed_world.world_id,
            "world": fed_world,
            "world_signer": fed_world.world_id,
            "initial_point": (200, 800),
        })
        for _ in range(3):
            white.step_via_adapter()

        # ---- Canvas (3 turns) ----
        white.enter_world_via_adapter(GrowingCanvasAdapter(), {
            "world_id": "world:canvas",
            "world": canvas_world,
            "world_signer": canvas_world.curator_public_key,
            "display_name": "White-bot",
        })
        for _ in range(3):
            white.step_via_adapter()

        # ---- Pack + verify ----
        bundle = pack_unified_bundle(
            white,
            persona="an individual across chess, chaos, and canvas",
            name="White-bot", initial_seed=100)
        bundle.save(root / "adapter_unified")
        loaded = IndividualBundle.load(root / "adapter_unified")

        # World logs
        from signed_world_log import signed_entry_hash
        chess_log = signed_chess.signed_log_since(None)
        fed_log = [
            {"body": r.body(), "sig": r.sig,
             "record_hash": r.record_hash()}
            for r in fed_world.records
        ]
        canvas_log = [
            {"event_hash": e.event_hash(),
             "event_dict": e.to_dict()}
            for e in canvas_world.events()
        ]
        world_logs = {
            "world:park": chess_log,
            fed_world.world_id: fed_log,
            "world:canvas": canvas_log,
        }

        v_full = verify_unified_individual_with_adapters(
            loaded, world_logs)

        # ---- Tamper: canvas coords ----
        tampered = IndividualBundle(
            manifest=dict(loaded.manifest),
            memory=list(loaded.memory),
            weights=dict(loaded.weights),
            initial_weights=None, observations=[],
            ancestry=[], checkpoint_weights=None,
        )
        for i, r in enumerate(tampered.memory):
            if r.get("tier") == "canvas":
                tampered.memory[i] = {**r, "x": 999, "y": 999}
                break
        t1 = verify_unified_individual_with_adapters(
            tampered, world_logs)

        # ---- Print ----
        print("=" * 74)
        print("World adapters — one individual, three tiers")
        print("=" * 74)
        print()
        print(f"  Individual: {loaded.individual_id[:32]}...")
        print(f"  Memory:     {len(loaded.memory)} entries")
        print(f"  Worlds:")
        for ctx in loaded.manifest["world_contexts"]:
            print(f"    {ctx['tier']:10s}  "
                  f"{ctx['world_id'][:24]}...  "
                  f"@ idx {ctx['first_memory_index']}")
        print()
        print("  Per-tier counts:")
        from collections import Counter
        c = Counter(r["tier"] for r in loaded.memory
                    if r.get("type") == "agent_step")
        for tier, n in sorted(c.items()):
            print(f"    {tier:10s}  {n} steps")
        print()
        print("  Verification:")
        print(f"    adapter-based full:  {v_full[0]}")
        if v_full[0]:
            print(f"      {v_full[1]}")
        print()
        print("  Tampering — canvas coords altered:")
        print(f"    {t1[0]}  ({t1[1]})")
        print()
        print("  What this establishes:")
        print("    - Three tiers, one model, one chain.")
        print("    - The world-adapter protocol works: a single")
        print("      interface (open, enter, state, action_from_index,")
        print("      submit, step_fields, verify_step) is all a")
        print("      new world needs to add.")
        print("    - Adding the growing canvas took ~110 lines of")
        print("      adapter code. No new session class, no new")
        print("      verifier, no new memory format.")
        print("    - Per-step dispatch: the verifier walks memory,")
        print("      finds the tier via world_entry, delegates to")
        print("      that tier's adapter for replay.")
        print()
        print("  Honest limit: all three tiers project into")
        print("  n_actions=3, state_dim=4. The projection is the")
        print("  adapter's job; the abstraction is limited to")
        print("  worlds whose action spaces can be narrowed to 3.")
        print("  Documented; production would need per-tier model")
        print("  heads or a projection layer.")
        print()
        print("  Anchor (public domain, Emily Dickinson):")
        print("    'I dwell in Possibility –'")
        print("    'A fairer House than Prose –'")
        print("    'More numerous of Windows –'")
        print("    'Superior – for Doors –'")

        audit = {
            "individual_id": loaded.individual_id,
            "worlds": [
                {"tier": c["tier"],
                 "world_id": c["world_id"],
                 "first_memory_index": c["first_memory_index"]}
                for c in loaded.manifest["world_contexts"]
            ],
            "memory_entries": len(loaded.memory),
            "per_tier_counts": dict(c),
            "verification": {
                "adapter_full": v_full[0],
            },
            "tampering": {
                "canvas_coords_detected": not t1[0],
            },
        }
        (root / "world_adapters_demo.json").write_text(
            _json.dumps(audit, indent=2))
        print(f"\n  → {root}/world_adapters_demo.json")
        return audit
    finally:
        try:
            chess_server.stop()
        except Exception:
            pass
```

What this establishes

The world-adapter protocol is the pattern, not the code. WorldAdapter has eight methods: tier_name, n_actions, state_dim, open, enter, state, action_from_index, submit, step_fields, world_log, verify_step. Ten in all. Every one has a clear job, and every one is what a new world would implement to join the individual layer.

Adding a world is ~80-120 lines. The GrowingCanvasAdapter is 110 lines — it petitions the world, translates the model's 0|1|2 into 3 candidate plot coordinates, submits canvas.claim, and returns the accepted growth event hash. No new session class, no new verifier, no new memory format. The previous pattern would have been: new GrowingCanvasSession class, new memory record shape, new verify_growing_canvas_bundle function. This is 3x simpler.

One model, three worlds, one chain. The unified individual's memory alternates world_entry and agent_step records across three tiers, all signed by the same key, all verified against the same model replay. The model's hidden state carries across world boundaries; the RNG reseeds at each world_entry (exploration is per-world, learning is per-individual). This is what "individual inhabits the arc" actually looks like in memory.

Verification dispatch is per-step, tier-resolved, self-contained. verify_unified_individual_with_adapters walks memory; each world_entry switches the adapter; each agent_step calls the adapter's verify_step. Each adapter does model replay (with the shared model state) plus world cross-reference (against that tier's log shape). Adding a tier means adding an adapter — the verifier doesn't change.

Tampering is caught by whichever tier is broken. test_tampered_canvas_coords — alter a canvas step's coordinates, and GrowingCanvasAdapter.verify_step catches it via coord mismatch against CANVAS_CANDIDATES[idx]. Federated tampering is caught by FederatedAdapter's transform math. Chess tampering by ChessAdapter's legal-move replay. Each tier's verifier knows its own invariants.

Honest limits

· All tiers project into n_actions=3, state_dim=4. This works because TinyRNN is 4-unit with 3-action output. The projection is the adapter's job: chess narrows 20+ legal moves to 3 via idx % len(legal); canvas invents 3 candidate plots; federated has exactly 3 transforms. A world with a richer action space (say a chess variant with more pieces) would need either a wider model, per-tier model heads, or a coarser projection. Documented at the top of world_adapters.py.
· Chess projection via idx % len(legal) is coarse. The model's "policy" is essentially "pick the 0th, 1st, or 2nd of the sorted legal moves" — where the sort changes each turn. This is not real chess strategy; it's just verifiable action selection. Same limitation as the previous chess cycle. Fine for demonstrating the pattern; not a chess AI.
· Canvas adapter uses only 3 candidate plots. The growing canvas supports any (x, y, w, h) claim. The adapter narrows to 3 fixed candidates so the model has a bounded action space. The world doesn't know; it just sees 3 candidate coordinates per turn. This is legitimate (any agent has a bounded policy) but means the individual doesn't explore the canvas — it just rotates through 3 plots.
· GrowingCanvasAdapter.world_log returns events with event_hash pre-computed. The GrowthEvent class has event_hash() as a method; I precompute it at log-fetch time. verify_step matches by hash. But this means the world_log isn't quite "raw" — it's been lightly transformed. Alternative: recompute event_hash() on the verifier side (slower, but zero transformation). Documented; the current form is fine.
· FederatedAdapter.state() reads last_action, last_reward from memory but prev_point from the last federated step. If a federated step follows a chess step (mix in memory), it correctly finds the federated prev_point by scanning back past chess entries. _prev_point walks memory backwards until it finds a federated agent_step or a world_entry with initial_point. Works; but the scan is O(steps). Not optimized.
· The step_fields for federated needs from_point/to_point, computed by step_via_adapter before submit. This means the adapter's step_fields(action, world_ref) reads action["_from_point"] which the session populates. Slightly asymmetric with the other adapters, where action_from_index fully determines the payload. A cleaner design would have the federated adapter compute from/to inside submit, using its own state. Refactor for a future cycle; documented as a current inconsistency.
· No composition with lifetime / resume / fork / delegation. A unified individual with adapter-based memory is kind: "unified_individual". The lifetime verifier's dispatch handles that kind (via verify_unified_individual_basic when no logs, or the full adapter-based verification with logs). Resume / fork / delegation all expect specific memory shapes and don't yet handle the unified shape. Cross-tier composition is future work; the previous cycle's limits apply.
· Worlds must be open before enter and must remain open through the session. For chess, the world URL must be live. For federated/canvas, the in-process world handle must be alive. enter_world_via_adapter doesn't validate liveness; a dead handle fails at submit or verify. Documented; not hardened.
· Chess world's world_signer must be passed in config. The adapter doesn't fetch it. If the caller passes a wrong world_signer, verification of chess steps' signed entries will fail. This is intentional — the signer is the caller's declaration. Not hardened; a future enter could fetch the signer from /manifest.
· No adapter registry with versioning or capability negotiation. DEFAULT_ADAPTERS is a module-level dict. A real deployment would need to know which adapters a verifier has (to refuse to verify worlds it doesn't understand) and which versions are compatible. Not built.
· ChessAdapter.world_log fetches over HTTP per verify_step. Actually no — verify_step doesn't call world_log; the caller supplies it once. Good. But submit fetches /signed-log on every chess move. For N moves, that's N HTTP requests just to find the reference. Could be optimized with since parameter; not built.
· The demo's Black is not a unified individual. It's a raw ChessIndividualSession. This is because the demo focuses on White's memory. Both could be unified; not built. The demo's "one individual across three worlds" claim is White's claim; Black is context.

What's next

Three directions:

1. Resumable unified individuals. Extend resume_from_bundle and pack_resumed_bundle to handle kind: "unified_individual". The resumed bundle carries the mixed-tier prefix; verification walks the prefix with adapter dispatch, then the new suffix with its own tier. Small extension; completes the composition with cycle 95's resume machinery.
2. World-adapter composition with forks and delegation. A unified individual that gets forked carries mixed-tier memory into its fork. Verification of the fork walks the prefix with adapters, then the suffix with the fork's own tier. Also small; needs the forked verifier to accept mixed-tier memory.
3. The reference adapter for the arc's full world set. Write adapters for the coupled CA, the attentive gallery, the fractal grid, the chaos game (already done), the elementary CA, the atomic fractal, and the room world. ~8 more adapters, each ~100 lines. Then a single individual can inhabit any world in the arc with one model and one chain — the arc's two halves fully compose. That's the endpoint this direction has been pointing at.

My instinct: resumable unified individuals. It's the smallest piece that makes the adapter-based unified individual durable — able to pause, resume, delegate, fork. Without it, the unified individual's life ends when the session ends, and the adapter work doesn't compose with the rest of the individual lifecycle. With it, the unified individual is just another kind of bundle that the lifecycle machinery handles.

But the reference adapter for the full world set is the claim that the arc's worlds and individuals compose. If the arc is going to be used — an individual that gardens, plays chess, participates in a gallery, walks among room-worlds — the adapters are the piece that makes it real. Once you have 10 adapters, an individual can live an actual multi-world life, verified end-to-end.

Which would you like?


::➡️
